questions.question: When making a U-turn:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake. It could cause the bike to tip over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake. It could cause the bike to tip over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it could cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn
No U-turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then apply it again quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight, even with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: You should keep a longer following distance:

options.text: If the pavement is slippery.
If traffic is light.
If you can see through the vehicles in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Keep more space between you and other vehicles when the pavement is slippery, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or when traffic is heavy. Use at least a four-second following distance in these conditions.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, maintain a following distance of at least:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between your bike and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down and downshift as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and ride away.
Swerve around the dog.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and downshift as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: When a dog approaches, slow down and downshift. Then quickly accelerate and ride away as the dog gets close.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Get closer to the vehicle in front of you to use its lights to see ahead.
Ride at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and keep more distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep more distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. You cannot see as far ahead, so you need more time and space to react to dangers.

questions.question: What is the best position to ride in within a lane?

options.text: The left position
The right position
There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: There is no single best position to ride in a lane. Good riders change their position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop completely and wait for a green light that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and do not brake.
Shift your weight to the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel and pull off the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and do not brake.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat while riding, grip the handlebars firmly and keep the motorcycle going straight. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road safely.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from flat mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, vehicles in convex mirrors appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Get closer to the vehicle ahead of you.
Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?

options.text: At the very front leading the group.
Near the front of the group, behind the leader.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group, behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, right behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch over the newer riders.

questions.question: When riding over textured pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down at the road surface to see the changes.
Look ahead and keep your head up.
Stay on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep your head up.
questions.explanation: When riding over textured pavement in a work zone, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, maintain a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: During daylight hours.
At dusk.
At night.

questions.correctAnswerText: During daylight hours.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur during daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials whenever you ride, even during the day.

questions.question: If you pass parked vehicles on your right and no traffic is coming toward you, where should you ride?

options.text: On the left side of your lane.
On the right side of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked vehicles and no oncoming traffic is present. This helps you avoid dangers like opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out. If traffic is coming, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you press the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How should you carry a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: Over the rear axle.
On the gas tank in front of you.
Stacked against the back of the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over the rear axle.
questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble," or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
The front wheel is not tightened properly to the frame.
The front tire hit an object.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven weight distribution.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. It is usually caused by improper weight distribution, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.
No, but it is recommended.
Only for new riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: When you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both at the same time.
Only brake.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center portion of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may make the driver return to your lane too soon, which is also dangerous.
